Analyzing data on the level of cognitive processes - ESCoP 2025

Gidon T. Frischkorn, Ruhi Bhanap, and Isabel Courage

Exercise 7: Signal Discrimination Model

In this exercise, we will have a look at fitting the Signal Discrimation model to a continous reproduction task varying the set size of to be remembered color patches.

# empty environment
rm(list = ls())

# load libraries
library("here")
library("tidyverse")
library("brms")
library("bmm")

The data is part of the bmm package and can be loaded as oberauer_lin_2017.

sdm_data <- oberauer_lin_2017
head(sdm_data)
## # A tibble: 6 × 19
##      ID session trial set_size dev_rad col_nt1 col_nt2 col_nt3 col_nt4 col_nt5
##   <dbl> <fct>   <dbl> <fct>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>

## 2     1 1           2 3        -0.454    0.855   1.95   NA       NA     NA    
## 3     1 1           3 5        -0.0873   0.716  -2.62   -1.03     1.38  NA    
## 4     1 1           4 6         0.367    0.262   2.04    0.105    1.10  -0.925
## 5     1 1           5 1        -0.0349  NA      NA      NA       NA     NA

## #   dist_nt2 <dbl>, dist_nt3 <dbl>, dist_nt4 <dbl>, dist_nt5 <dbl>,
## #   dist_nt6 <dbl>, dist_nt7 <dbl>

Your task is:

  1. specify the sdm model object using the response error dev_rad.
sdm_model <- sdm(resp_error = "dev_rad")
  1. estimate an sdm model evaluating if the parameter c or kappa changes over set size. Consider entering set size as a numeric variable assuming a linear set size effect
sdm_data$ss_num <- as.numeric(sdm_data$set_size)

# center on set size 1
sdm_data$ss_num <- sdm_data$ss_num - min(sdm_data$ss_num)

# sort data by predictor for faster fitting
sdm_data_sorted <- sdm_data %>% arrange(ss_num, ID)

sdm_formula <- bmf(
  c ~ 1 + ss_num + (1 + ss_num | ID),
  kappa ~ 1 + ss_num + (1 + ss_num | ID)
)

default_prior(sdm_formula, data = sdm_data, model = sdm_model)
##                     prior     class      coef group resp  dpar nlpar   lb   ub
##                    lkj(1)       cor                                           
##                    lkj(1)       cor              ID                           
##              normal(0, 1)         b    ss_num                c       <NA> <NA>
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd                          c          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd              ID          c          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd Intercept    ID          c          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd    ss_num    ID          c          0     
##              normal(0, 1)         b    ss_num            kappa       <NA> <NA>
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd                      kappa          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd              ID      kappa          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd Intercept    ID      kappa          0     
##      student_t(3, 0, 2.5)        sd    ss_num    ID      kappa          0     
##              normal(0, 1)         b                          c       <NA> <NA>
##     student_t(5, 2, 0.75) Intercept                          c       <NA> <NA>
##              normal(0, 1)         b                      kappa       <NA> <NA>
##  student_t(5, 1.75, 0.75) Intercept                      kappa       <NA> <NA>
##               constant(0) Intercept                                  <NA> <NA>

  1. fit the sdm to the data
sdm_fit <- bmm(
  formula = sdm_formula,
  data = sdm_data_sorted,
  model = sdm_model,
  # sampler settings
  cores = 4,
  init = 0.5,
  iter = 2000,
  refresh = 100,
  sample_prior = TRUE,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  file = here("models","exc7_sdm_setsize")
)

brms::pp_check(sdm_fit)

  1. plot the predicted effects on c and kappa using the conditional_effects function
conditional_effects(sdm_fit, dpar = "c", effects = "ss_num")

conditional_effects(sdm_fit, dpar = "kappa", effects = "ss_num")

  1. use the hypothesis function to test for effects of set size on c and kappa
ss_effects <- hypothesis(
  sdm_fit,
  c("c_setsize" = "c_ss_num = 0",
    "kappa_setsize" = "kappa_ss_num = 0")
)
ss_effects
## Hypothesis Tests for class b:
##      Hypothesis Estimate Est.Error CI.Lower CI.Upper Evid.Ratio Post.Prob Star
## 1     c_setsize    -0.24      0.01    -0.27    -0.21       0.00      0.00    *
## 2 kappa_setsize    -0.02      0.01    -0.05     0.01      29.35      0.97     
## ---
## 'CI': 90%-CI for one-sided and 95%-CI for two-sided hypotheses.
## '*': For one-sided hypotheses, the posterior probability exceeds 95%;
## for two-sided hypotheses, the value tested against lies outside the 95%-CI.
## Posterior probabilities of point hypotheses assume equal prior probabilities.
plot(ss_effects)

If you want compare your results to fitting a two-parameter mixture model on the data. Again, see how the proportion of responses from memory and kappa is affected by the set size variable.

mixture_model <- mixture2p(resp_error = "dev_rad")

mixture_formula <- bmf(
  thetat ~ 1 + ss_num + (1 + ss_num | ID),
  kappa ~ 1 + ss_num + (1 + ss_num | ID)
)

mixture_fit <- bmm(
  formula = mixture_formula,
  data = sdm_data,
  model = mixture_model,
   # sampler settings
  cores = 4,
  init = 0.5,
  iter = 2000,
  refresh = 100,
  sample_prior = TRUE,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  file = here("models","exc7_mixture2p_setsize")
)

pp_check(mixture_fit)

summary(mixture_fit)
##   Model: mixture2p(resp_error = "dev_rad") 
##   Links: mu1 = tan_half; kappa = log; thetat = identity

##          total post-warmup draws = 4000
##

conditional_effects(mixture_fit, dpar = "theta1", effect = "ss_num")

conditional_effects(mixture_fit, dpar = "kappa1", effect = "ss_num")

hypothesis(
  mixture_fit,
  c("pMem_ss" = "thetat_ss_num = 0",
    "kappa_ss" = "kappa_ss_num = 0")
)
